value.body: A hotel management trainee follows a structured programme, rotating through departments such as front office, food and beverage, housekeeping and kitchen before taking a supervisory role in one of them. Hotel groups run these programmes and hire mostly from hotel management campuses. A typical day is working shifts in the current department under a manager.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: BHM or a B.Sc in Hospitality

items.label: Departments you rotate through
items.value: Front office, food & beverage, housekeeping and kitchen

items.label: BHM enrolment
items.source: AISHE 2023-24, Ministry of Education (programme-wise enrolment, all modes)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Selection is usually through campus placement, with group discussions and interviews. Seats are limited and competitive, and trainees are often expected to relocate.

value.title: At a glance
items: After the programme, trainees usually become assistant managers or supervisors in one department.
Willingness to relocate is often a condition.
Hours are long and include weekends and holidays.

value.title: Hotel management degree enrolment
value.note: Based on institutions that responded to AISHE; similar courses are recorded under several programme names, so totals here are partial.
value.source: AISHE 2021-22, 2022-23 and 2023-24 reports, Ministry of Education (programme-wise enrolment, all modes)
